liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Stuck In Side Of Mobile With The Memphis Blues Again** (4 reviews): Weir feigned forgetting the lyrics to coax Dylan into stepping up to sing; Weir sang until the 'two cures' line, refusing the mic; Dylan came up late and took over [16][18][19][25]
- **Cold Rain And Snow** (1 review): Opener described as fluid but slightly too polite [23]
- **Monkey And The Engineer** (1 review): Surprised the crowd by appearing for the first time in 17 years [24]
- **Alabama Getaway** (1 review): Garcia fumbled it slightly, but made up for it with nice playing [18]
- **The Other One** (1 other source): Kodo drummer Yoshikazu Fujimoto joined the band during Drums and The Other One [2]
- **Foolish Heart** (1 review): Oddly placed as the closer and, in this reviewer's view, thoroughly botched [19]
- **Knockin' On Heaven's Door** (1 review): Dylan returned to sing on the closing encore [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1989-02-12.sbd.miller.89200.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 154 min; rated 4.5/5 by 4 [1]
- **gd1989-02-12.fob.french.31265.sbeok.flac24**: source not stated; 22 songs; 160 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [7]
- **gd1989-02-12.fob.french.sirmick.76126.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 154 min [8]
- **gd1989-02-12.137005.sbd.miller.flac24**: soundboard; 21 songs; 156 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [2]

## Around the show

- Dylan, reportedly very drunk, joined in, seemed to be steering the setlist, and contributed little at first [16]
- Dylan sat in from Monkey And The Engineer through the Memphis Blues number [17]
- Hart's drumming was erratic and off the beat for most of the show, per the reviewer [19]
- Dylan had said while rehearsing for the 1987 stadium tour that he mainly wanted to play along with the Dead; he seemed to be enjoying himself here, not drunk [20]
- Parking-lot rumors predicted guests such as Dylan and Stephen Stills; most such rumors were usually wrong [24]
- A good video of this show is in circulation, according to the reviewer [25]
- Spencer Davis played guitar and sang on How Long Blues and Gimme Some Lovin' [2]
- Dylan played guitar and sang from Iko Iko through Memphis Blues, and on the Not Fade Away and Heaven's Door encores [2]
- This version lacks the excitement and youthful energy of the 1987 versions, according to the reviewer [23]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1989-02-12.sbd.miller.89200.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Dat (48k) [1]
- **gd1989-02-12.fob.french.31265.sbeok.flac24**: taped by Mike French; source: Sean Weber Small rig, Schoeps cmc?? (cardioid caps on mic bodies)ORTF -> Oade pre (m118?) -> Sony F1/Beta rig, line out -> Sony TC-D5M analog cassette master… [7]. Also: Taped from the same spot as the 2-10-89 and 2-11-89 shows and the December 1989 Forum run [7]
- **gd1989-02-12.fob.french.sirmick.76126.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Mike French; transferred by 16 bit conversion by SirMick; source: Sean Weber Small rig, Schoeps cmc?? (cardioid caps on mic bodies) ORTF -> Oade pre (m118?) -> Sony F1/Beta rig, line out -> Sony TC-D5M analog cassette master… [8]. Also: Same taping spot as the other 1989 Forum shows, including 2-10, 2-11 and the December run; Two recordings were spliced to complete Heaven's Door; the last 2:08 comes from the Neuman source; Transfer downsampled to 16/44.1 with Adobe Audition and dithered with iZotope Ozone; a sub-second track gap was removed [8]
- **gd1989-02-12.137005.sbd.miller.flac24**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [2]
